channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Power
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Attackers crossed from a wind farm into an unrelated Polish CHP plant over a private cellular APN — and stopped its steam turbine
item.description: CERT Polska has disclosed that attackers reached the control network of a Polish combined heat and power plant serving roughly 50,000 residents by pivoting through a private cellular APN, and stopped a steam turbine and the plant’s process-water treatment system. The intrusion started somewhere else entirely: a compromised FortiGate firewall at a wind farm, and a Teltonika cellular router on that network which reached a private APN operated by the distribution system operator. Because devices on that APN were permitted to talk to one another, the attacker crossed from one generator’s network into another operator’s controllers. CERT Polska believes this is the first observed real-world use of a private APN as a route into an industrial control network. Plant staff restored the affected systems quickly and customers saw no loss of supply. - CERT Polska disclosure — via Help Net Security, BleepingComputer and The Hacker News - Incident Dec 2025; disclosed 8 Aug 2026, analysis published 11–13 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] The Iranian-affiliated PLC campaign is an energy-sector problem too, and at one victim the actors disabled safety shutdown logic
item.description: Joint advisory AA26-097A — issued 7 April by the FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA, DOE, US Cyber Command’s Cyber National Mission Force and Treasury, and substantially expanded on 22 July — covers Iranian-affiliated actors reaching internet-exposed programmable logic controllers across US water, energy and government facilities. Two details matter for power operators. First, the observed manufacturer scope now runs beyond Rockwell Automation to Schneider Electric and Siemens controllers, so a utility that standardised away from MicroLogix is not automatically outside it. Second, at one confirmed US victim the actors modified ladder logic to disable safety shutdown and alarm functions, letting unsafe conditions develop without alerting operators. The agencies also documented project-file exfiltration and Dropbear SSH persistence. No CVE is involved: the entry path is exposure plus default, shared or absent credentials. - CISA/FBI joint advisory AA26-097A — corroborated by SecurityWeek - Issued 7 Apr 2026, updated 22 Jul 2026; campaign ongoing through mid-Aug 2026

item.title: [High] The multistate utility PLC attacks have reached at least 12 states — and many of those utilities also run the electric system
item.description: Water and wastewater systems in at least 12 states have reported operational-technology intrusions since late July, with more than 30 Minnesota community systems affected, a boil-water advisory in Clayton County, Georgia after a pump-station failure, and confirmed incidents in Michigan, South Dakota, New Jersey and Alabama. This belongs on a power page for a structural reason: a large share of the affected utilities are combined municipal utilities that run water, wastewater and electric distribution, frequently on shared network infrastructure, shared cellular contracts and a single small IT team. The technique used against the water side — find a controller answering from the internet, change its IP address, set a password the operator does not have — works identically against a recloser controller, a substation gateway or a distribution RTU. - The Record and Axios, citing state officials and the FBI - Campaign since 26–27 Jul 2026; tally reached 12 states 4–12 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Clop has named 43 PTC Windchill victims including Shell and GE, and what it took is engineering data
item.description: The Clop extortion group has listed 43 organisations on its leak site after a mass data-theft campaign against internet-exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM product-lifecycle instances, exploiting CVE-2026-12569, an improper input validation flaw. Ransom-ISAC assesses with high confidence that Clop affiliates ran it as a zero-day in early June, weeks before PTC began issuing patches on 17 June. Clop claims 89 GB from Shell, including engineering drawings, facility test reports and project plans; Philips has confirmed an enterprise server breach it says was contained, and GE says it is assessing the claim. BleepingComputer reports Clop built a custom web shell for the campaign. For energy operators the exposure is not the plant floor but the design record — drawings, test reports and vendor configuration that make a later, targeted intrusion far easier. - Clop leak-site listings — reported by BleepingComputer and TechTimes - Exploited from early Jun 2026; victims named 15–17 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] CISA added the exploited vCenter flaw to KEV on 18 August — the campaign has hit 361 hosts in 47 countries
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-59310, a path-traversal flaw in VMware vCenter Server, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 18 August. Broadcom patched it on 29 July; exploitation started roughly five days later. German incident-response firm QUIRSO assesses with moderate confidence that a Chinese-speaking actor is behind the campaign, based on Chinese-language artefacts in the attacker’s scripts and tooling, and counts about 361 affected addresses across 47 countries, with Germany, the United States, Turkey, Iran and France most represented. The actor obtains root on the vCenter appliance, installs a backdoor via cron and a reverse SSH binary, and in at least one case deployed Babuk-derived ransomware. Utilities that host EMS, historian or engineering-workstation virtual machines on vCenter should treat this as an OT-adjacent exposure, not an IT one. - CISA KEV catalogue and QUIRSO research — via The Hacker News - Patched 29 Jul 2026; exploitation from early Aug; added to KEV 18 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] A joint advisory names utilities among Gunra ransomware’s targets, and the way in is unpatched edge devices
item.description: CISA, the FBI, NSA, DC3, the Secret Service and South Korea’s National Police Agency issued #StopRansomware advisory AA26-222A on 10 August covering Gunra, a double-extortion operation built on leaked Conti source code that moved to a ransomware-as-a-service affiliate model in 2026. The sector list explicitly includes utilities, critical manufacturing, transportation and government facilities. What makes it actionable rather than merely alarming is the initial access: Gunra affiliates are exploiting CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472 in internet-facing FortiOS and FortiProxy devices — both long-patched authentication bypasses that grant super-admin and defeat multi-factor authentication. Nothing novel is required. The advisory ships detection content and indicators, which makes this a straightforward hunt rather than a research project. - CISA #StopRansomware advisory AA26-222A - Published 10 Aug 2026

item.title: [Critical] SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced ships a Node-RED interface with no authentication — unauthenticated code execution at maximum severity
item.description: In its August Patch Tuesday round Siemens published ten advisories, the most serious of which (SSA-834709) covers SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed. The Node-RED HTTP interface does not enforce authentication, so a remote unauthenticated attacker can reach programming nodes that execute system commands and create flows that run arbitrary code on the device with maximum privileges. Siemens rates it at the top of the scale and has released a fixed version. IoT2050 gateways are common in energy applications as edge data-collection and protocol-translation points between substation or generation equipment and a historian or cloud service, which means a device that is trusted by the control network but frequently managed outside it. - Siemens ProductCERT SSA-834709 — via SecurityWeek - Published 11 Aug 2026 (August ICS Patch Tuesday)

item.title: [Critical] A CVSS 10.0 command injection gives unauthenticated root on Haiwell’s IoT Cloud HMI gateway
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-225-02 covers CVE-2026-19188, an OS command injection in the Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway rated 10.0. The Net Check feature reached through the /setting endpoint passes user-supplied input from the cmdPing Socket.io event to the operating system without sanitisation, so an unauthenticated remote attacker can run arbitrary commands as root. Version 3.40.1.12 is affected and Haiwell has published Scada-v3.50.1.19 as the fix. Haiwell gear turns up in smaller generation sites, DER installations and balance-of-plant systems where it was chosen on cost, and it is exactly the class of device that ends up on a cellular connection for remote monitoring — the same pattern behind this month’s utility intrusions. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-225-02 - Published 13 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] CISA’s 13 August batch of 15 advisories lands squarely on energy gear: Hitachi Energy, Johnson Controls and ANDRITZ
item.description: CISA published fifteen ICS advisories on 13 August, several of them directly relevant to generation and transmission. ICSA-26-225-04 covers Hitachi Energy APM Edge versions 6.10 and earlier, where CVE-2026-43284 and CVE-2026-43500 — write-what-where conditions in the Linux kernel’s IPsec ESP subsystem — let a local unprivileged user escalate to root. ICSA-26-225-03 covers a hardcoded password or cryptographic key in the Johnson Controls Airwall application, with v4.1.0 or later recommended for all Airwalls; Airwall is deployed precisely to segment and protect OT, so a hardcoded secret undercuts a control many utilities rely on. Advisories for ANDRITZ HIPASE-250 and 250 SCALA protection and control platforms are in the same batch. - CISA ICS advisories, 13 Aug 2026 batch — roundup via WaterISAC and Industrial Cyber - Published 13 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Cisco ASA and Firepower Threat Defense joined CISA’s KEV catalogue on 11 August
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-20349, a heap inspection vulnerability in Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and Firepower Threat Defense, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 11 August, alongside a Windows Ancillary Function Driver use-after-free and a Metabase SQL injection flaw. The KEV listing means confirmed exploitation in the wild, not theoretical risk. ASA and FTD appliances sit at the boundary of many utility networks and terminate the VPN tunnels that vendors, integrators and on-call engineers use to reach EMS, SCADA and substation networks. A compromise there does not just expose data; it hands an attacker the same access path your own engineers use, with the same reach into the control environment. - CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue - Added to KEV 11 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] Yesterday’s CISA advisories cover a Simcenter stack overflow and CISA’s own Malcolm analysis suite
item.description: CISA published two ICS advisories on 18 August. ICSA-26-230-02 covers CVE-2026-59086, a stack overflow in Siemens Simcenter Femap and Simcenter Nastran before version 2606: an affected binary reading an arbitrary string as a file argument can be made to execute code in the context of the current process if a user is persuaded to run it with a malicious input. ICSA-26-230-01 covers several flaws in CISA Malcolm, the agency’s own network traffic analysis suite, which is widely used for passive OT monitoring — denial of service or code execution across a set of CVEs fixed in releases up to and beyond 26.07.1. Engineering and analysis workstations sit close to the control network and are frequently outside the OT patch cycle. - CISA ICS advisories ICSA-26-230-01 and ICSA-26-230-02 - Published 18 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] CIP-012-2 is in force, CIP-003-9 has been enforceable since April, and the 2026 roadmap points at low-impact and cloud
item.description: Two compliance dates have already passed this year and both change day-to-day practice. CIP-003-9 became enforceable on 1 April, extending governance expectations to low-impact BES cyber systems with an explicit focus on vendor remote access and supply chain. CIP-012-2 took effect on 1 July, tightening protection of real-time operational data exchanged between control centres. Looking ahead, NERC’s CIP Roadmap published in January sets out near-term standards work and widens the scope conversation to low-impact systems, cloud services, telecommunications and DER aggregators, while FERC has directed NERC to extend internal network security monitoring under CIP-015 to EACMS and PACS. Penalties remain up to $1 million per violation per day, but the operational point is that low-impact sites and vendor access are where the next audit attention lands. - NERC CIP Roadmap (Jan 2026) and standard effective dates — summarised by Ampyx Cyber and Tenable - CIP-003-9 effective 1 Apr 2026; CIP-012-2 effective 1 Jul 2026; roadmap Jan 2026

item.title: [Low] A Senate letter asks Treasury to stop the tax code penalising OT security spending
item.description: Senator Tom Cotton wrote to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on 5 August asking that federal tax guidance be adjusted so it encourages rather than discourages modernisation of the operational technology that runs critical infrastructure, citing the Minnesota water attacks and the Iranian PLC campaign as the prompt. Three specific asks: confirm that security software for industrial control systems qualifies as research under Section 41; use Section 7701(e) to create a safe harbour so cybersecurity monitoring agreements with public utilities are treated as services rather than long-term equipment leases; and extend the existing lease exception to service providers, since a firm that retains ownership of security equipment and sells monitoring gets no equivalent protection today. Nothing has changed yet, but the financing friction behind slow OT security adoption is now on the record. - Senator Cotton’s office — reported by FedScoop and Industrial Cyber - Letter sent 5 Aug 2026
